comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Sizing RCA before push: the current 1 GiB constant is under-sized. On current origin/main with the exact macOS selectors, 3 workers, required extras, and explicit basetemps, the default tier retained 1,138,012 KiB across 233,910 files; integration passed 167/2-skipped and retained 1,139,044 KiB across 25,863 files. Keeping both trees consumes 2,277,056 KiB (2.171 GiB), so neither 1 GiB nor 2 GiB with both trees satisfies the >=50% headroom AC. The integration footprint is dominated by the intentional 141 MiB incompressible partial-clone fixture replicated across xdist workers. Because the tiers run sequentially, the safe repair is to use a 2 GiB APFS volume, report and remove the exact successful default basetemp before integration, then retain the integration tree until always-run final reporting/detach. This keeps each tier's measured ~1.086 GiB peak below 2 GiB with ~87% headroom and preserves a failed default tree for diagnostics because later success-only steps do not run after failure. No selector, test, worker, timeout, platform, assertion, or coverage behavior changes.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Phase-1 runtime RCA from Gerrit 1806 PS1 run 31869753711: the macOS default suite itself passed 13,397/65-skipped in 1,123.77s, then the release step spent about 47.3s recursively measuring 1,128,280 KiB / 231,474 files and failed during rm -rf. The failing paths are tests/unit/workflow snapshot fixtures whose production contract deliberately chmods published snapshot directories/files read-only (src/rebar/llm/workflow/snapshot.py); hosted macOS emitted Permission denied for those exact .rebar/run_snapshots paths, left DEFAULT_BASETEMP nonempty, and skipped integration. The always-run final reporter still detached exact /dev/disk8 successfully, so no device leaked. Confirmed mechanism: the new success-path release assumes pytest basetemp is recursively removable, but the suite intentionally leaves owner-nonwritable snapshot trees; restore owner write permission recursively on the already exact-path-validated DEFAULT_BASETEMP before removal. This is a cleanup-contract defect, not a test assertion failure. Separately, this first treatment sample was slower than control (18m43s default versus 17m26s exact control), so RAM-disk efficacy remains unproven pending the already-running duplicate/organic samples; do not treat the cleanup repair as performance proof.

comments.body: Retention decision: reject and revert the RAM-disk experiment. RAM-disk run 31869753711 completed the same 13,397/65-skipped default in 18m43.77s (about 7.5% slower), then spent 71s measuring/removing and failed on intentionally read-only snapshot trees. Independent organic change 1807 run 31869919362 completed 13,425/65-skipped in 20m54.61s, then spent 98s in the same failed release step. Every observed treatment is slower, none clears the predeclared larger-of-5%-or-variation improvement threshold, and recursive observability/release itself adds material runner occupancy. Per AC7 the experiment must not be retained. Change 1806 is being amended to restore runner.temp and remove the RAM-disk lifecycle and its contract test; selectors, markers, workers, timeouts, platforms, coverage, assertions, collection, and integration coverage remain unchanged.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body: Patchset 3 secondary CI RCA: Gerrit Verify run 31872498514 failed its unchanged default suite on Ubuntu 3.11 and 3.12 because the new held-out cleanup oracle launched nested pytest with cacheprovider enabled. Nested pytest inherited the checkout as root and created .pytest_cache; the outer full-suite command deliberately disables its own cacheprovider, so tests/conftest.py correctly reported a new REPO_ROOT entry. Local exact reproduction with outer -p no:cacheprovider was RED with that leak. Adding -p no:cacheprovider to the nested process returned GREEN; deleting the flag returned the exact RED, and restoring it returned GREEN again. Focused snapshot/repo-isolation coverage passed 18 tests, make lint including all-workflow actionlint and release zizmor passed, and patchset 4 run 31873067707 is active. This changes test hygiene only; selectors, assertions, workers, platforms, coverage, and behavioral scope remain unchanged. Patchset 3 was superseded and canceled within 76 seconds of patchset 4 creation.

comments.author: RebarBotNava
comments.body:
Final rebar-debug report after Gerrit 1806 merged as commit 7d908fbbc6da12f8e274b3ef1e3a2357377799ef.

Problem — determine whether moving the unchanged macOS pytest trees to an APFS RAM disk reduces Gerrit Verify critical-path and runner time without changing fidelity.

Proven result and classification — the storage hypothesis is rejected for this workload. The implementation followed maintained OSS precedent from Apple Git CI, Aeron, and Git performance guidance, but it was an optimization experiment rather than a product defect. Rebar measurements override that directional precedent: the exact no-RAM control 31868300174 ran the default suite in 17m26s and the macOS job in 20m36s; RAM-disk treatments ran the same default suite in 18m43.77s, 20m54.61s, 18m26s, and, on final green patchset-4 run 31873067707, 20m00.60s. Every treatment was slower than control and none met the predeclared retention oracle.

Proof — treatment runs 31869753711, 31869919362, 31870391571, and 31873067707 independently falsified the prediction that storage placement would reduce wall time. Recursive observability/release also added 71-98 seconds; the final live run spent about 88 seconds between the 20m00.60s default result and integration start. The evidence rejects runner-temp filesystem latency as the dominant explanation and rejects retaining the RAM-disk lifecycle.

Tests and secondary repairs — the first treatment exposed intentionally owner-nonwritable workflow snapshot fixtures that made ordinary recursive basetemp cleanup raise PermissionError. The held-out subprocess oracle in tests/unit/test_ci_snapshot_fixture_cleanup.py was RED without per-test teardown, GREEN with teardown, RED again under the exact-defect mutation, then GREEN after restoration. Patchset 3 exposed a separate nested-pytest cacheprovider leak; exact outer -p no:cacheprovider reproduction was RED, adding the same flag to the nested process was GREEN, removing it returned RED, and restoring it returned GREEN. Focused snapshot/isolation tests passed 18 tests.

Fix — merged change 1806 removes the RAM-disk setup, reporting, recursive release, and detach lifecycle; restores both unchanged pytest tiers to runner.temp; removes the experiment-only workflow contract; and retains only the test-local snapshot cleanup plus held-out regression.

Scope and safety — selectors, markers, assertions, xdist worker counts/distribution, timeouts, Python/platform matrix, coverage-once behavior, integration tier, and collection remain unchanged. No dependency was added and no existing assertion was weakened. Merged workflow lines 651 and 666 route distinct default and integration basetemps under runner.temp.

Siblings — no other production sibling was found. The only observed cleanup siblings were the snapshot permission contract and nested cacheprovider leak, both fixed in scope. Workflow parity is not applicable beyond the single matrix workflow; Ubuntu remained byte-for-byte on runner.temp throughout the experiment.

Residual risk and disposition — accepted: final run 31873067707 necessarily executed the trusted-main RAM-disk workflow, so the restored no-RAM path needs several organic post-merge full runs before any 20-30 minute average claim. This remains tracked by parent runtime ticket inedible-subsimious-brahmancow. The N=3000 import long pole remains separately tracked by ravenous-beribboned-walleye.

Replication and gates — run 31873067707 passed all four full suites and the exact hosted macOS cleanup path that previously failed; macOS completed in 24m42s, the workflow concluded success, LLM-Review +1 and Verified +1 were present, zero unresolved comments remained, and Gerrit 1806 merged at 2026-08-15T08:20:32Z. The merged tree contains no RAM-disk lifecycle and both basetemps are back under runner.temp.

## Context and evidence

The remaining macOS critical path is filesystem-heavy. The N=3000 import long pole reproduces at 20.19-21.63s on the same macOS host with 15.39-16.65s system CPU versus 4.59-5.67s user CPU. cProfile attributes 13.69s to 24 required git-add/git-commit pairs, while the full default suite creates thousands of temporary Git stores below pytest --basetemp. The workflow deliberately uses runner.temp rather than /tmp because the macOS tmp cleaner previously deleted live test trees.

Maintained OSS precedent matches this mechanism. Apple Git CI creates a 4GB APFS RAM disk for test output and documents greater-than-2x test speedup from avoiding slow storage for many small writes (apple-oss-distributions/Git src/git/.gitlab-ci.yml lines 82-88 at 6b2f9bfe). Aeron creates a macOS APFS RAM disk in GitHub Actions for its temporary test filesystem (aeron-io/aeron .github/workflows/ci.yml lines 62-68 at 092f184a). Git t/perf/README says putting test roots on tmpfs can massively speed the suite. Tracker search found no prior RAM-disk/tmpfs proposal or rejection. This changes storage placement only: no test, worker, platform, behavioral assertion, coverage, mutation work, or runner is removed or added.

Operator direction: do not land a control-only patchset, because an extra full-matrix run would create the contention this work is intended to reduce. Use the next full Verify run initiated by another session as the timing control. Storage sizing comes from the stable local full-suite temp tree or one local explicit-basetemp reproduction; only an implementation change may trigger another Gerrit run.

## Plan

1. Watch the next unrelated full Gerrit Verify run for ambient context without modifying it, and use a no-extra-run trusted-workflow control only when its selectors and collection/pass/skip counts match the treatment. Capture macOS default/integration/job and Ubuntu job wall times, slow-duration tail, queue delay, run conclusion, checked-out patchset, and collection counts. The primary control ultimately captured as 31868300174 used runner.temp and matched the first treatment at 13,397 passed / 65 skipped default and 158 passed / 11 skipped integration; unrelated-run timings remain contextual rather than causal proof.
2. Measure retained temp allocated bytes and file count from a stable local full-suite run using the same selectors and distinct explicit basetemps. Size the RAM disk with at least 50% headroom while keeping it below 40% of detected runner physical memory. If the requirement cannot fit, stop and report infeasibility rather than risk memory pressure or a full volume.
3. In the existing build/test matrix job, create an APFS RAM disk only when runner.os is macOS, after setup/gates and immediately before pytest. Publish its exact device and /Volumes/RebarTests mount path through step outputs; /Volumes is outside the /tmp and /var/folders locations subject to the macOS tmp cleaner. Non-macOS cells continue using runner.temp byte-for-byte. Route both unchanged pytest selectors to separate basetemps below that mount.
4. Always report filesystem type, allocated bytes, file count, and capacity, then detach the exact device created by setup after both pytest tiers, including failure/cancellation paths where GitHub permits cleanup. Do not use a broad disk target, persistent mount, cache, extra runner, or extra job.
5. Add static workflow contract tests proving macOS-only creation, measured bounded sizing, unchanged selectors/xdist worker counts/timeouts/coverage flags, distinct default/integration basetemps, and always-run exact-device cleanup. Explicitly re-run the existing workflow consumers tests/unit/test_ci_workflow_parity.py, tests/unit/test_gate_step_tree_skew.py, tests/unit/test_extra_coverage_guard.py, and tests/unit/test_worktree_python_pin.py; these consumers should remain unchanged unless an existing invariant truly changes. Run actionlint and zizmor.
6. Push the implementation through Gerrit immediately. Compare matched selector/collection-count treatments primarily with exact no-RAM control 31868300174 and secondarily with recent green runs; report absolute/percentage savings and Ubuntu non-regression. Retain only if the full matrix is green and both macOS default-suite and job wall times improve by at least the larger of 5% or the observed recent-green range. Worked 5% floor from the exact 17m26s default / 20m36s job control: treatment must be at most 16m33.7s default and 19m34.2s job before any larger observed-range requirement; otherwise revert the lifecycle.

## Test contract card

authoritative_contract: .github/workflows/_build-and-test.yml executes the unchanged default and integration pytest selectors on Ubuntu 3.11/3.12/3.13 and macOS 3.13, with coverage once on Ubuntu 3.13.
trigger_preconditions: macOS matrix cell reaches the pytest steps after all existing gates.
production_path: GitHub Actions creates an ephemeral APFS RAM device, pytest tmp_path/basetemp writes real Git repositories there, then cleanup detaches only that device.
test_tier: static workflow contract tests plus the actual full Gerrit Verify matrix.
observable_postcondition: identical collection/pass/skip counts and gates, lower macOS pytest/job wall time, bounded RAM use, no mounted device after cleanup.
negative_control: every Ubuntu cell keeps runner.temp and existing behavior; a RAM-disk setup/sizing failure fails loudly before tests rather than silently changing coverage.
collateral_invariants: no test selection, assertion, marker, worker count, timeout, coverage, mutation shard, Python/platform cell, or runner concurrency changes.
ci_gate: actionlint, zizmor, workflow contract tests, full Gerrit Verify, LLM-Review.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The next unrelated full Verify run records control macOS default/integration/job wall times, Ubuntu job times, queue delay, slow tail, and conclusion without a control-only patchset.
- [ ] Local retained-temp evidence yields at least 50% RAM-disk headroom below 40% of detected physical memory.
- [ ] The selected outcome is platform-safe: if retained, only macOS creates and uses the APFS RAM disk while Ubuntu retains runner.temp; if rejected by the AC7 retention oracle, the RAM-disk lifecycle is absent and every cell uses runner.temp.
- [ ] Default and integration selectors, markers, xdist counts/distribution, timeouts, coverage-once behavior, collection/pass/skip counts, and all platform/Python cells remain unchanged.
- [ ] If the RAM-disk outcome is retained, cleanup runs under always(), reports final filesystem usage, and detaches only the exact device created by setup; if rejected by AC7, no RAM-disk cleanup lifecycle remains.
- [ ] Static workflow tests, actionlint, zizmor, focused/full pytest, LLM-Review, and Gerrit Verified are green.
- [ ] Against a no-RAM control with matching selectors and collection/pass/skip counts, both macOS default-suite and job wall times are lower than control by at least the larger of 5% or the observed recent-green range, with no Ubuntu regression; otherwise the experimental lifecycle is fully reverted. For the captured 17m26s default / 20m36s job control, the 5% floor is at most 16m33.7s default and 19m34.2s job before applying any larger observed-range requirement.
